item.title: Go Daily Question 205
item.description:
What is the output of the following code and why?

func hello() []string {  
    return nil
}

func main() {  
    h := hello
    if h == nil {
        fmt.Println("nil")
    } else {
        fmt.Println("not nil")
    }
}
  • A. nil
  • B. not nil
  • C. compilation error
🔑 Answer Analysis:

B

hello is a Function value. Functions are first-class citizens in Go. Therefore, if h == nil is valid. Since function values have a value (an address), they are also not nil. Functions are also values. They can be passed around like other values. Function values can be used as function arguments and return values.

item.title: Go Daily Question 195
item.description:
What is the flaw in the following code:

func sum(x, y int)(total int, error) {
    return x+y, nil
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

Answer: The second return value is not named.

Analysis:

When a function has multiple return values, if one return value is named, all others must also be named. If there are multiple return values, they must be enclosed in parentheses (); if there is only one named return value, it must also be enclosed in parentheses (). Here, the first return value total is named, but the second one is not, which is an error.

item.title: Go Daily Question 121
item.description:
What will the following code output?

func increaseA() int {
    var i int
    defer func() {
        i++
    }()
    return i
}

func increaseB() (r int) {
    defer func() {
        r++
    }()
    return r
}

func main() {
    fmt.Println(increaseA())
    fmt.Println(increaseB())
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

0 1 The difference between the two functions above is that increaseA() has an anonymous return parameter, while increaseB() has a named one. For A, executing return i assigns the value of i to the return parameter, and the subsequent i++ does not affect it. For B, executing return r assigns r to r. The subsequent r++ affects it because it’s the same r.

item.title: Go Daily Question 074
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

package main

import "fmt"

func app() func(string) string {
    t := "Hi"
    c := func(b string) string {
        t = t + " " + b
        return t
    }
    return c
}

func main() {
    a := app()
    b := app()
    a("go")
    fmt.Println(b("All"))
    fmt.Println(a("All"))
}

A: Hi All; B: Hi go All; C: Hi; D: go Al

🔑 Answer Analysis:

Closure fmt.Println(b("All")) outputs A (Hi All) fmt.Println(a("All")) outputs B (Hi go All)

item.title: Go Daily Question 058
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

func incr(p *int) int {
    *p++
    return *p
}

func main() {
    p :=1
    incr(&p)
    fmt.Println(p)
}
  • A. 1
  • B. 2
  • C. 3
🔑 Answer Analysis:

Answer: B.

Key takeaway: Pointers. p in the incr() function is a pointer of type *int, pointing to the address of the variable p in the main() function. The second line of code performs an increment operation on the value at that address. incr() returns the result after the increment.

item.title: Go Daily Question 035
item.description:
What is the output of the following code and why?

func hello() []string {  
    return nil
}

func main() {  
    h := hello
    if h == nil {
        fmt.Println("nil")
    } else {
        fmt.Println("not nil")
    }
}

A. nil B. not nil C. compilation error

🔑 Answer Analysis:

B. In this problem, the function hello is assigned to variable h, rather than the return value of the function (i.e., it’s not a function call). Therefore, the output is not nil. Note that functions are first-class citizens in Go.

item.title: Go Daily Question 006
item.description:
What is the flaw in the following code:

func sum(x, y int)(total int, error) {
    return x+y, nil
}
🔑 Answer Analysis: 
Answer: ``(total int, error)`` the second return value error is not named.

Analysis:
When a function has multiple return values, if one return value is named, all others must also be named.
``func sum(x, y int)(total int,err error) {`` If there are multiple return values, they must be enclosed in parentheses ().
``func sum(x, y int)(total int,err error)``
``func sum(x, y int)int`` If there is only one return value and it is named, it must also be enclosed in parentheses (). ``func sum(x, y int)(total int) {``

Here, the first return value `total` is named, but the second one is not, which is an error.
